summary:
[  edit  ]
The Cache  TOP  stores a sequence of images into  GPU  memory. These cached images can be read by the graphics card much faster than an image cache in main memory or reading images off disk.
The Cache  TOP  can be used to freeze images in the  TOP  by turning the Active parameter Off. (You can set the cache size too  1 .)
The Cache  TOP  acts as a delay if you set Output Index to negative numbers and leave the Active parameter On.
Once a sequence of images has been captured by turning the Active parameter On or toggling the Active  Pulse  parameter, they can be looped by animating the Output Index parameter.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: While this is On, the Cache  TOP  will capture images into its memory.

parameters.label: Active  Pulse
parameters.name: activepulse
parameters.description: Captures an image for the single frame this was pulsed.

parameters.label: Get One Image on Startup
parameters.name: cacheonce
parameters.description: Checking this On will cook the  TOP  once after startup to load an initial image.

parameters.label: Replace Single
parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: While this is On, the Cache  TOP  will replace the image at 'Replace Index' with the input image. This allows you to replace specific images in the cache at will.

parameters.label: Replace  Pulse
parameters.name: replacespulse
parameters.description: Replace an image for the single frame this was pulsed.

parameters.label: Replace Index
parameters.name: replaceindex
parameters.description: Select the image index that will be replaced by the input, when 'Replace Single' is turned on.

parameters.label: Pre-Fill
parameters.name: prefill
parameters.description: Cooks 'Cache Size' number of times to fill the Cache  TOP  with images. When set to 1, it will fill the cache. If set to 1 during playback, it will fill immediately. If set to 1 and saved out, then next time the file is opened the cache will pre-fill. While this is > 0, the node behaves as if the Active parameter is Off. If set to 0, then back > 0, it will clear the previous data, and pre-fill again. For more information refer to the  Pre-Filling  article.

parameters.label: Pre-Fill  Pulse
parameters.name: prefillpulse
parameters.description: Pre-fills a single image during the frame this was pulsed.

parameters.label: Cache Size
parameters.name: cachesize
parameters.description: Determines the number of images that can be stored in this Cache  TOP .

parameters.label: Step Size
parameters.name: step
parameters.description: The number of cooks that go by before the Cache  TOP  grabs an image. A Step Size of 2 will cache an image every 2nd cook, a Step Size of 3 will cache every 3rd cook, and so on.

parameters.label: Output Index
parameters.name: outputindex
parameters.description: Determines which image in cache the  TOP  outputs. 0 is the most recent image, negative integers output image further back in time.

parameters.label: Output Index Unit
parameters.name: outputindexunit
parameters.description: Sets the units used in the Output Index parameter.

parameters.label: Interpolate Frames
parameters.name: interp
parameters.description: When On (On = 1), the Cache  TOP  will interpolate between frames when non-integer values are used in the Output Index parameter. For example, a value of -0.5 in Output Index will output a blended image of the most recent frame (0.0) and the second most recent frame (-1.0).

parameters.label: Always  Cook
parameters.name: alwayscook
parameters.description: Forces the operator to cook every frame.

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: While On this will empty the cache of stored images and release the memory held by the  TOP .

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: Instantly empty the cache.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. Making this larger than 1 is essentially the same as taking the output from each pass, and passing it into the first input of the node and repeating the process. Other inputs and parameters remain the same for each pass.

Cache Blend POP * **¿Qué hace?** Este operador se conecta a un Cache POP y te permite **mezclar diferentes conjuntos de datos guardados en caché** por ese Cache POP. * **Características clave:** * Requiere una referencia a un **Cache POP** como fuente de datos. * La mezcla se realiza **por cada punto individualmente**, lo que significa que el resultado de un punto no depende de los otros puntos en la mezcla. * Es muy útil para crear **"desenfoques de tiempo"** en datos de g
